'''Marcin Maciej Hoffmann''' (born October 2, 1972) is a Polish [[scientist]] and [[Entrepreneurship|entrepreneur]]. He is a professor of chemistry at the Faculty of Chemistry of [[Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań]].

== Early years ==
Hoffmann was born in 1972 in [[Godziesze Wielkie]], a small town near [[Kalisz]]. He attended No. 30 Primary School in Poznań and the [[Karol Marcinkowski High School|Karol Marcinkowski High School in Poznań]]; at that time, he succeeded as a laureate of Polish Physics Olympiad and twice as a laureate of Polish Chemistry Olympiad. In 1996, he was awarded the [[Master of Science|MSc]] in Chemistry title at the Faculty of Chemistry of [[Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań]]; his [[thesis]] ''Theoretical analysis of selected [[Tartaric acid|(R,R)-tartaric acid]] [[Derivative (chemistry)|derivatives]]'', supervised by Jacek Rychlewski, was awarded the first prize in Faculty's Contest for the best MSc dissertation of that year. In 1997, he achieved MSc in Biotechnology at the [[Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań|AMU]] Faculty of Biology for his thesis ''Properties of [[glycoprotein]]s isolated from [[Chelidonium majus]] [[Sap|milky sap]]'', supervised by Anna Goździcka-Józefiak. During his MSc courses he won a number of various [[scholarship]]s, including ones granted by the [[Ministry of National Education (Poland)|Minister of National Education]].<ref>Responsible for higher education in Poland at that time.</ref> and [[Stefan Batory Foundation|the Stefan Batory Foundation]], he was also the President of Student Council at the [[Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań|AMU]] Faculty of Chemistry.{{sfn|Hoffmann|2014}} In 2000, he defended his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] thesis in chemistry, ''Effects of [[Substituent|substitution]] of [[Hydroxy group|hydroxyl group]] by [[Fluorine|fluorine atom]] - [[Ab initio quantum chemistry methods|ab initio]] and [[Density functional theory|DFT]] studies''<ref>{{Polish scientists|91253}}</ref> (under the supervision of Rychlewski), rewarded with the first prize in annual Faculty's Contest for the best PhD dissertation. He also completed an [[Master of Business Administration|MBA]] degree, organized jointly by [[Poznań University of Economics and Business|Poznań Academy of Economics]] and [[Georgia State University|Georgia State University in Atlanta]] in 2000 (with Henryk Mruk as the tutor of his managerial project) and [[Postgraduate education|postgraduate studies]] in [[computer science]] at the [[Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań|AMU]] Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science in 2004.{{sfn|Hoffmann|2014}}

== Academic career ==
Already during his [[Master of Science|MSc course]], Hoffmann took an academic internship at the [[University of Oxford]] under Dr John M. Brown.{{sfn|Hoffmann|2014}} Upon receiving his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD degree]], he was employed as [[assistant professor]] at the [[Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań|AMU]] Faculty of Chemistry; in 2001–2002, he worked as a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral fellow]] at [[Emory University|Emory University in Atlanta]], where he conducted research under the supervision of [[Keiji Morokuma]],{{sfn|Hoffmann|2014}} a globally recognized expert in [[quantum chemistry]].<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Cui, Q |author2=Irle, S. |author3=Musaev, J. |date=February 2018|title=Keiji Morokuma (1934-2017)|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition|volume=57|issue=9|pages=2288–2289|doi=10.1002/anie.201800390|pmid=29392802|doi-access=free}}</ref> As a young scientist, he was awarded a number of [[scholarship]]s by various institutions, such as the [[Foundation for Polish Science]] and the Centre for Applied [[Quantum mechanics|Wave Mechanics]] (''Centre de Mécanique Ondulatoire Appliquée'').{{sfn|Hoffmann|2014}} He defended his [[Habilitation|habilitation thesis]] ''[[Computational chemistry|Quantum-chemical calculations]] in [[molecular modelling]] of selected systems of importance in [[chemistry]], [[biochemistry]], and [[medicine]]''<ref>{{Polish scientists|91253}}</ref> in 2009 and became an [[associate professor]] two years later. On March 8, 2017, at the age of 44, he was conferred [[Professor|the professor title]] by [[Andrzej Duda]], [[President of Poland|the President of the Republic of Poland]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.prezydent.pl/aktualnosci/nominacje/art,50,prezydent-wreczyl-nominacje-profesorskie.html|title=Prezydent wręczył nominacje profesorskie|date=2017-03-08|website=prezydent.pl|language=pl|trans-title=The President conferred professor titles|access-date=2018-10-29|archive-date=2017-12-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171211064222/http://www.prezydent.pl/aktualnosci/nominacje/art,50,prezydent-wreczyl-nominacje-profesorskie.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

=== Scientific activity ===
Hoffmann's research focuses on the application of [[Computational chemistry|computational methods of quantum chemistry]] in the investigation of the [[Molecular geometry|structure of molecules]] and the [[Intermolecular force|interactions between them]], as well as [[Molecular modelling|modelling]] of [[Enzyme catalysis|enzymatic reactions]] along with [[Drug design|designing novel drugs]] and [[chemical compound]]s of desirable [[Biological activity|activity]] with the use of [[computational model]]s built for this purpose. The results of his scientific research include:

* Determination of the effect of [[Substituent|substitution]] of [[Hydroxy group|hydroxyl group]] by [[Fluorine|fluorine atom]] in a series of compounds, including [[Tartaric acid|(R,R)-tartaric acid]] [[Derivative (chemistry)|derivatives]] and [[Glucose|D-glucose]], on their [[Conformational isomerism|conformational freedom]].<ref>{{Cite journal|author1=Hoffmann, M. |author2=Rychlewski, J. |author3=Rychlewska, U. |date=February 1999|title=Effects of Substitution of OH Group by F Atom for Conformational Preferences of Fluorine-Substituted Analogues of (R, R)-Tartaric Acid, Its Dimethyl Diester, Diamide, and N, N, N ', N '-Tetramethyl Diamide. Ab Initio Conformational Analysis|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=121|issue=9|pages=1912–1921|doi=10.1021/ja982935+}}</ref><ref name="pmid11456879">{{cite journal|author1=Hoffmann, M. |author2=Rychlewski, J. |date=March 2001|title=Effects of substituting a OH group by a F atom in D-glucose. Ab initio and DFT analysis|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=123|issue=10|pages=2308–16|doi=10.1021/ja003198w|pmid=11456879}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|author1=Hoffmann, M. |author2=Rychlewski, J. |date=July 2002|title=When, in the context of drug design, can a fluorine atom successfully substitute a hydroxyl group?|journal=International Journal of Quantum Chemistry|volume=89|issue=4|pages=419–427|doi=10.1002/qua.10277}}</ref>
* Detailed [[Conformational isomerism|conformational analysis]] of multiple [[Tartaric acid|(R,R)-tartaric acid]] [[Derivative (chemistry)|derivatives]].<ref>{{Cite journal|author1=Szarecka, A. |author2=Hoffmann, M. |author3=Rychlewski, J |author4=Rychlewska, U. |date=January 1996|title=X-ray diffraction and theoretical studies of the methyl ester of (R,R)-tartaric acid monoamide: semiempirical and ab initio calculations of some model compounds|journal=Journal of Molecular Structure|volume=374|issue=1–3|pages=363–372|doi=10.1016/0022-2860(95)08928-4|bibcode=1996JMoSt.374..363S}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|author1=Gawroński, J. |author2=Gawrońska, K. |author3=Skowronek, P. |author4=Rychlewska, U. |display-authors=etal|date=April 1997|title=Factors affecting conformation of (R, R)-tartaric acid ester, amide and nitrile derivatives. X-ray diffraction, circular dichroism, nuclear magnetic resonance and ab initio studies|journal=Tetrahedron|volume=53|issue=17|pages=6113–6144|doi=10.1016/S0040-4020(97)00271-8}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|author1=Rychlewska, U. |author2=Warżajtis, B. |author3=Hoffmann, M. |author4=Rychlewski, J. |date=July 1997|title=(R, R)-Tartaric Acid Dimethyl Diester from X-Ray and Ab Initio Studies: Factors Influencing Its Conformation and Packing|journal=Molecules|volume=2|issue=7|pages=106–113|doi=10.3390/20700106|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|author1=Hoffmann, M. |author2=Szarecka, A. |author3=Rychlewski, J. |year=1998|title=Gas-phase Conformational Analysis of (R, R)-Tartaric Acid, its Diamide, N, N, N′, N′-Tetramethyldiamide and Model Compounds|volume=32|pages=109–125|doi=10.1016/S0065-3276(08)60409-8|series=Advances in Quantum Chemistry|isbn=9780120348336}}</ref>
* Detailed explanation of the [[Reaction mechanism|mechanism]] of [[Squalene monooxygenase|squalene epoxidase]] [[Enzyme inhibitor|inhibition]] by [[terbinafine]] and elucidation of a fully atomic three-dimensional model of this [[protein]].<ref name="pmid21229992">{{cite journal|author1=Nowosielski, M. |author2=Hoffmann, M. |author3=Wyrwicz, L.S. |author4=Stepniak, P. |display-authors=etal|date=February 2011|title=Detailed mechanism of squalene epoxidase inhibition by terbinafine|journal=Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling|volume=51|issue=2|pages=455–62|doi=10.1021/ci100403b|pmid=21229992}}</ref>

Quantum chemical study on the reaction of azathioprine with cysteine|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=123|issue=26|pages=6404–9|doi=10.1021/ja010378c|pmid=11427067}}</ref>

These and other studies resulted in authorship and co-authorship of ca. 100 [[Scientific literature#Scientific article|publications]] (101 according to [[Google Scholar]]), including highly prestigious [[scientific journal]]s, such as [[Journal of the American Chemical Society]] and [[Cancer Research (journal)|Cancer Research]]. His papers are increasingly [[Citation|cited]] year after year (totalling 960 - [[Google Scholar]]), which yields 9,50 citations per publication and the [[h-index]] of 18.<ref>{{Google Scholar id|6p-9FNMAAAAJ}}</ref>

=== Educational activity ===
Since 1996, Hoffmann has been actively teaching at the [[Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań|AMU]] Faculty of Chemistry, partly in English. These classes include lectures, seminars, proseminars and laboratory exercises in a wide range of courses, from fundamental subjects, namely [[physical chemistry]], [[quantum chemistry]] and [[theoretical chemistry]], to more specific ones, such as the application of [[Computational chemistry|computational methods]], [[molecular modelling]] and [[online database]]s in other [[Chemistry#Subdisciplines|branches of chemistry]]. He also worked as a teacher in X High School in [[Poznań]] for two years (1999-2001).{{sfn|Hoffmann|2014}} During his career he has supervised several tens of [[Bachelor's degree|bachelor's]] and [[Master's degree|master's]] [[Thesis|theses]], as well as four [[Thesis|doctoral dissertations]]:<ref>{{Polish scientists|91253}}</ref>

* Dr [[Jakub Paś]] (2013), dissertation title: ''Application and implementation of [[Probability theory|probabilistic]] profile-profile comparison methods for [[Protein structure prediction|protein fold recognition]]''.
* Dr Marcin Nowosielski (2015), dissertation title: ''[[Quantum mechanics|Quantum]] and [[classical mechanics]] [[Computational chemistry|computational methods]] in [[Drug design#Computer-aided drug design|computer-aided drug design]].''
* Dr Wojciech Jankowski (2017), dissertation title: ''[[Quantum chemistry|Quantum-chemical]] studies of [[Coordination complex|complexes]] of selected [[alkaloid]]s with [[Zinc|zinc(II)]] and [[Copper|copper(II)]] [[ion]]s.''
*Dr Martyna Kuta-Siejkowska (2018), dissertation title: ''Studies on interactions of [[Protooncogene|protooncogenic]] [[G-quadruplex]]es with [[ligand]]s.''

He has also reviewed several tens of bachelor's and master's theses, seven doctoral dissertations, two habilitation processes and two applications for the professor title (by Dr hab. Mariusz Makowski, [[Uniwersytet Gdański|UG]] and Dr hab. Robert Wieczorek, [[Uniwersytet Wrocławski|UWr]]).

=== Organizational activity ===
For many years, Hoffmann has been actively working for the expansion of [[Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań|Adam Mickiewicz University's]] scientific and educational abilities, for example by initiating and co-authoring ''AMU – supranational and interdisciplinary solutions of 21st century'' ([[Polish language|pl.]] ''UAM – ponadnarodowe i interdyscyplinarne rozwiązania XXI wieku'') – a project co-funded by the [[National Centre for Research and Development in Poland|National Centre for Research and Development]], carried out in cooperation with the [[University of Massachusetts Lowell]], and co-authoring [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]], [[Master of Science|MSc]] and [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] course programmes at the Faculty of Chemistry. He vigorously participates in organizing [[Popular science|science popularization events]] at the Faculty, such as [[Poznań]] Festival of Science and Art or [[European Researchers' Night]]. Since 2012, he has been serving as [[Dean (education)|Deputy Dean for Research]] (re-elected in 2016).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://chemia.amu.edu.pl/glowna/wchem/struktura-wydziau/samodzielni-pracownicy-naukowi/prof.-uam-dr-hab.-marcin-hoffmann|title=Faculty of Chemistry of Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań - Marcin Hoffmann|language=pl|access-date=2018-10-29|archive-date=2018-09-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180914165545/https://chemia.amu.edu.pl/glowna/wchem/struktura-wydziau/samodzielni-pracownicy-naukowi/prof.-uam-dr-hab.-marcin-hoffmann|url-status=dead}}</ref> He is the initiator of and the [[Secretary (title)|Secretary]] of the [[Juried (competition)|Jury]] awarding [[Jacek Rychlewski]] Prize of the [[Polish Chemical Society]] for the best [[Thesis|MSc thesis]] on [[quantum chemistry]] or [[Computational chemistry|exploiting quantum chemistry methods in other branches of science]]. He has reviewed and issued opinions on the implementation of research projects funded by the [[The National Science Centre (Poland)|National Science Centre]], applications for grants for young scientists and project applications submitted to [[Polish Grid Infrastructure PL-Grid|Polish Grid Infrastructure PLGrid]]. In 2013, in cooperation with [[BioInfoBank Institute]] and [[Interdisciplinary Centre for Mathematical and Computational Modelling]], Hoffmann organized an [[Academic conference|international conference]] ''Advances in [[Molecular modelling|Molecular Modelling]]''. Since 2014, he is a member of the Scientific Committee of ''All-Polish PhD Students' Seminar "Between Chemistry and Biology"'' ([[Polish language|pl.]] ''Ogólnopolskie Seminarium Doktorantów „Na pograniczu chemii i biologii”'').<ref name="www.npcib.pl">{{Cite web|url=http://www.npcib.pl/commitees.php|title=XVI Na pograniczu chemii i biologii 2018 - Organizatorzy|trans-title=XVI Between Chemistry and Biology - Organizers|access-date=2018-10-29}}</ref> He also [[Chairman|chaired]] the proceeding of [[Theoretical chemistry|theoretical]] and [[computational chemistry]] section during the 59th Scientific Congress of the [[Polish Chemical Society]] in 2016.<ref name="ptchem2016.amu.edu.pl">{{Cite web|url=http://ptchem2016.amu.edu.pl/index.php/sekcje-zjazdu|title=59 Zjazd Naukowy Polskiego Towarzystwa Chemicznego - Sekcje Zjazdu|trans-title=59th Scientific Congress of the Polish Chemical Society - Sections|access-date=2018-10-29}}</ref>

== Other achievements ==
Aside from his academic work, Hoffmann has been widely cooperating with [[High tech|high-tech enterprises]], implementing the idea of [[Knowledge economy|knowledge-based economy]], for almost twenty years. In 2002–2003, he worked as [[McKinsey & Company]] consultant, managing [[telecommunication]]s and [[energy carrier]]s; in 2004, he became the Director for Investments & Development at [[BioInfoBank Institute]]. In 2007, together with Leszek Rychlewski, he founded [[BIB Seed Capital]] - a [[Seed money|seed capital fund]] focused on supporting [[Poland|Polish]] scientific and engineering thought in such fields as [[bioinformatics]], [[molecular biology]], [[chemistry]] and [[computer science]], along with facilitating [[Technology transfer|its transfer]] to [[small and medium-sized enterprises]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://seed.bioinfo.pl/en/|title=BIB Seed Capital|access-date=2018-10-29}}</ref> Well-aimed [[investment]]s of the company, led by Hoffmann to the present day, allowed it to multiply its [[Financial capital|financial resources]], and some of the [[Startup company|startups]] it had funded became global players, such as:

* Medicalgorithmics S.A. – a Polish [[High tech|high-tech]] company, an expert in and a supplier of systemic and [[Algorithmics|algorithmic]] solutions in [[Cardiology diagnostic tests and procedures|cardiac diagnosis]]; the company is listed on the [[Warsaw Stock Exchange]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.medicalgorithmics.com/|title=Medicalgorithmics|access-date=2018-10-29}}</ref>
* Proteon Pharmaceuticals S.A. – a Polish [[Pharmaceutical industry|pharmaceutical company]], which carries out research of [[bacteriophage]]s and uses them as a basis for developing novel [[Pharmaceutical formulation|formulations]] - successful substitutes for [[antibiotic]]s<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.proteonpharma.com/|title=Proteon Pharmaceuticals|access-date=2018-10-29}}</ref>

Since 2010, he has worked as [[expert witness]] of the [[Judiciary of Poland|District Court in Poznań]] in [[exact sciences]], [[Economics|economic sciences]] and [[Company|enterprise]]; he has also issued expert opinions for courts in other cities, including [[Warsaw]], [[Myślibórz]] and [[Łowicz]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.poznan.so.gov.pl/download/lista-bieglych-24.08.2018-r.-internet.pdf|title=Lista biegłych sądowych Sądu Okręgowego w Poznaniu|language=pl|trans-title=The register of expert witnesses of District Court in Poznań|access-date=2018-10-29}}</ref>
